title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 248 (Power of Registrar to remove name of company)

content.overview: Section 248 lets the Registrar strike off a company that is not carrying on business or has not filed for the stated period, and lets a defunct company apply for removal of its name.
content.glance: Section 248 lets the Registrar strike off a company that is not carrying on business or has not filed for the stated period, and lets a defunct company apply for removal of its name.
content.study: The Registrar may send notice where the company has failed to commence business within one year of incorporation, has not been carrying on business for two financial years and has not applied for dormant status, or where subscribers have not paid and the declaration under the commencement provision has not been filed. The company may itself apply, after extinguishing liabilities, where it is not carrying on business. Notice is published and objections are considered. A company is not to be struck off if, in the preceding three months, it has changed its name, shifted registered office, disposed of property otherwise than in the ordinary course, engaged in any activity other than what is necessary for the application, applied for compromise, or been wound up. Strike-off does not erase liability of directors and officers. Restoration is under s. 252.

sections.heading: Ingredient 1
sections.body: A ground in s. 248(1) or a company application under s. 248(2)

sections.heading: Ingredient 3
sections.body: No bar in s. 248(3) if the company is applying

sections.heading: Rule
sections.body: The Registrar may send notice where the company has failed to commence business within one year of incorporation, has not been carrying on business for two financial years and has not applied for dormant status, or where subscribers have not paid and the declaration under the commencement provision has not been filed. The company may itself apply, after extinguishing liabilities, where it is not carrying on business. Notice is published and objections are considered. A company is not to be struck off if, in the preceding three months, it has changed its name, shifted registered office, disposed of property otherwise than in the ordinary course, engaged in any activity other than what is necessary for the application, applied for compromise, or been wound up. Strike-off does not erase liability of directors and officers. Restoration is under s. 252.

examples.title: Non-filing
examples.body: Two years without business and without dormant-company status can support a Registrar notice.

examples.title: Recent sale
examples.body: A property sale outside the ordinary course in the preceding three months bars a company-initiated strike-off.

hypotheticals.facts: Two years without business and without dormant-company status can support a Registrar notice.
hypotheticals.analysis: Section 248 lets the Registrar strike off a company that is not carrying on business or has not filed for the stated period, and lets a defunct company apply for removal of its name.

distinctions: Strike-off is an administrative removal of name. Winding up is a collective insolvency or Tribunal process. Restoration under s. 252 can revive the company as if the name had not been struck off.

misconceptions.correction: Section 248 lets the Registrar strike off a company that is not carrying on business or has not filed for the stated period, and lets a defunct company apply for removal of its name.

questionsAndAnswers.question: Does strike-off end the directors' liability for past debts?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: No. Section 248 preserves the liability of officers and members to the extent stated.
